goal.objective:
Finish the resolver in `src/`. `src/index.js` re-exports `ResolveError`, `parseVersion`, `compareVersions`, `parseRange`, `satisfies` and `maxSatisfying` from `src/semver.js` and `ConflictError` and `resolve` from `src/resolve.js`; keep that surface. `ResolveError` extends `Error`, sets `name` to `'ResolveError'`, carries a `code` and is constructed as `(code, message)`. A version is exactly three numeric parts with no leading zeros and no suffix; `parseVersion` returns `{ major, minor, patch }` and otherwise throws `'BAD_VERSION'` with message `invalid version: <text>`. `compareVersions(left, right)` returns -1, 0 or 1 by comparing the three parts numerically, so `1.10.0` is above `1.9.0`.

`parseRange(text)` turns a range into the list of comparators that must all hold, each `{ operator, version }` with an operator of `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` or `=`. Whitespace around the range is ignored and one or more spaces separate conjuncts. `*` alone means no comparators at all and may not appear beside anything else. A bare version, or one written with `=`, is an equality comparator. `^V` means at least `V` and below the next version that changes the leftmost non-zero part: `^1.2.3` spans up to but excluding `2.0.0`, `^0.2.3` up to `0.3.0`, and `^0.0.3` up to `0.0.4`. `~V` means at least `V` and below the next minor, so `~1.2.3` spans up to `1.3.0`. Anything else, including an empty range, a lone operator, an operator separated from its version by a space, or an unparseable version, throws `'BAD_RANGE'` with message `invalid range: <text>`. `satisfies(version, range)` tests one version against every comparator, and `maxSatisfying(versions, range)` returns the highest satisfying version of a list or null.

`resolve(registry, rootDeps)` picks exactly one version per package. The registry maps a package name to an object of versions, each version to metadata whose optional `deps` maps a package name to a range. It is validated up front: a non-object registry throws `'BAD_REGISTRY'` with message `registry must be an object`, a non-object package entry gives `registry entry must be an object: <name>`, every version key must parse, non-object metadata gives `metadata must be an object: <name>@<version>`, and a dependency map that is not an object throws `'BAD_DEPENDENCIES'` with message `dependencies of <name>@<version> must be an object`. The root map is validated the same way, with `root dependencies must be an object`, and every range in either place must parse.

Resolution keeps a list of constraints per package and a set of pending packages, seeded from the root dependencies taken in ascending name order, where each root constraint records the origin `<root>`. While anything is pending, take the lexicographically smallest pending name and select it: a name absent from the registry throws `'UNKNOWN_PACKAGE'` with message `unknown package: <name>`; otherwise the candidates are the registry's versions of that package that satisfy every constraint recorded for it so far, and the highest candidate wins. Selecting a package at a version gives it a chain, which is the origin recorded with its first constraint followed by ` > <name>@<version>`, so a root dependency `a` chosen at 1.0.0 has the chain `<root> > a@1.0.0`. Its dependencies are then walked in ascending name order: each adds a constraint whose origin is the selecting package's chain, and a dependency that has not been selected becomes pending, while one that is already selected must still satisfy the new range. A package with no satisfying candidate, and a selected package that a later constraint contradicts, both raise `ConflictError`, which extends `ResolveError`, sets `name` to `'ConflictError'` and `code` to `'CONFLICT'`, and carries `packageName`, `available` (that package's versions in ascending order) and `constraints`, the recorded constraints as `{ range, via }` in the order they arrived. Its message is `cannot satisfy <name>: ` followed by those constraints as `<range> (from <via>)` joined with `, `. On success the result is `{ resolved, order }`, where `resolved` maps names to versions in ascending name order and `order` lists the names in the order they were selected. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
